analogs.covers: Solo buck: a ram living apart from the band, waiting for the head-ramming duel that wins him females
Terrain: a cliff dweller that never strays far from defensible rock

solo.headline: A lone bighorn ram on the cliffs: exiled from the band, he shadows it from a distance and waits for his chance to ram the lead buck.
solo.playsLike: Solo you are almost always an adult buck. As soon as your mature colours show you are chased from the band, even by your mother, and you cannot group with other adult males. You follow bands at a distance, waiting to challenge their buck, keep a strong sense of escape routes and rarely stray from defensible terrain. Out of boredom or curiosity you may trail other herbivores, but you never become part of their herd; only at night you may settle quietly near a sleeping herd and use its bulk as a shield. Alone you are at much higher risk of being picked off. A solitary female, by contrast, always wants to get back into a band.

why.text: Maturing males are “chased from the band to begin life as solitary bucks”. Bighorn rams leave the ewes and live apart until the rut.
Rival males linger on the outskirts of bands, waiting for the chance to challenge the buck, then settle it head to head like rutting rams.
“Even solitary individuals display a strong awareness of escape routes and rarely stray far from defensible terrain.” That is the mountain goat's cliff sense.
Only at night will a loner settle near a resting herbivore, “using their bulk as a shield against the dark”.

notLike: Bighorn rams form bachelor bands outside the rut; adult Pachycephalosaurus bucks cannot group with other adult males.
It eats berries, but also carrion and bones.
solo.summary: Solo bist du fast immer ein erwachsener Bock, also ein einsamer Dickhornwidder an den Klippen. Sobald deine Erwachsenenfarben kommen, jagt dich die Band davon, sogar die eigene Mutter, und mit anderen erwachsenen Böcken darfst du dich nicht zusammentun. Du folgst Bands mit Abstand und wartest auf die Gelegenheit, ihren Bock herauszufordern. Wie eine Schneeziege kennst du immer deinen Fluchtweg und bleibst nah an sicherem Fels. Aus Langeweile läufst du manchmal anderen Pflanzenfressern hinterher, gehörst aber nie dazu. Nur nachts legst du dich leise neben eine schlafende Herde. Eine einzelne Geiß will dagegen immer zurück in eine Band.
